notes: Machine-checked by scripts/check-harvest.mjs, which runs inside the required Provenance boundary context.

coverageRoots enumerate every place a capability can live. Every path under a root must be claimed by exactly one row, so adding a capability without a ledger row turns the gate red instead of passing silently.
Findings are recorded separately from capabilities: a finding has no path, so it cannot participate in coverage.

capabilities.title: Composition decision core
capabilities.rationale: Decides whether two intents may compose. That is a prescriptive judgment, and GOVERNANCE.md rejects prescriptive policy from the standard. Harvesting it upstream would be the charter violation META-284 is unwinding.

capabilities.title: Authorization receipt and lifecycle contract
capabilities.rationale: The lifecycle another agent system can adopt without adopting Interlock's policy. The contract travels; the decision does not. EXECUTED and OBSERVED must not collapse in any harvested form.

capabilities.title: Interlock enforcement proxy
capabilities.rationale: Reference-application enforcement path proven by HAC-326. Product, not seam.

capabilities.title: Protected target service
capabilities.rationale: The mutation surface the proxy protects. Exists to make the counterfactual demonstrable; not reusable outside it.

capabilities.title: Bypass guard, idempotency ledger, revision binding
capabilities.rationale: Fail-closed primitives bound to this broker's semantics. HAC-317 owns any production generalization; nothing is proposed for a workspacejson repository.

capabilities.title: Independent observation and correlation
capabilities.rationale: Emits the state chain the cockpit renders. Travels conceptually with the receipt contract but is not separately harvestable.

capabilities.title: Runtime configuration and JSON transport
capabilities.rationale: Ordinary application plumbing. Recorded so coverage is complete, not because it is notable.

capabilities.title: Four-arm evaluation harness
capabilities.rationale: Arms, corpus, executor and aggregation for a multi-condition comparison where every arm can fail. Carries the freeze-before-results protocol and the packet verifier in the same tree.

capabilities.title: Evidence provenance envelope and pinned-upstream adapter
capabilities.rationale: Wraps a verbatim upstream result with producer SHA, package version, bundle digest, source revision, history basis and artifact digest, and refuses to run against a dirty or off-pin checkout. The synthetic-history fixtures in the same tree are superseded by META-383's use of real history and are not part of the harvest.
supersededParts: experiments/hac-330/bin/build-fixtures.mjs generates synthetic Git histories; META-383 replaced the approach with real repository history. Deleted post-window with the rest of the tree's fixture machinery.

capabilities.title: Public evidence redaction and logged-out verification
capabilities.rationale: Redacts a packet for publication and verifies it resolves logged out. Bound to this submission's disclosure boundary; generalizing it would mean generalizing that boundary.

capabilities.title: S2 fallback enforcement path
capabilities.rationale: The proven bounded MCP/API proxy enforcement path. Its production successor is HAC-317's scope inside this repository; nothing here is proposed for any workspacejson repository.

capabilities.title: Filmed-run capture and verification
capabilities.rationale: Builds and verifies a filmed run against its scene manifest. Studio v3 is already the consumer, so this is a harvest with a live customer.

capabilities.title: Agent Gateway provisioning scripts
capabilities.rationale: Belongs to a path recorded as FAILED/PIVOTED. Keeping executable provisioning for an abandoned architecture invites someone to run it. HAC-338 owns the forensic finding; the scripts are not needed to preserve it.

capabilities.title: Judge verification cockpit
capabilities.rationale: The judge-facing surface for pinned runs, including the cold-read kit. Product.

capabilities.title: Evidence-bound architecture visual suite
capabilities.rationale: Generates architecture and proof visuals from machine-readable state. test/hac-334-gate-perturbation.test.mjs travels with it: a pipeline that cannot demonstrate its own gate failing is the vacuous-green case META-337 eliminated. bin/lib/motion.mjs extends the same library with a time axis — semantic and presentation tracks, deterministic state-at-time, and a reduced-motion equivalent — earned by HAC-350 needing a frame at t that does not depend on having played the cut. It is Interlock-agnostic and harvests with the rest of the suite.

capabilities.title: Judge package and asset registry
capabilities.rationale: Binds every exported asset to an asset ID, judge question, source run, supported claim, runtime source SHA and evidence-publication SHA. The general capability is evidence-bound media.

capabilities.title: Evidence-bound final cut assembly
capabilities.rationale: Composes a cut from an authored edit decision list and frozen artifacts, and gates the result against them: an input manifest with content digests, a scene map from timestamp to source artifact to claim, and a render manifest read back out of the encoded file. The general capability is an edit that cannot outrun its evidence, which is the same Studio customer as hac-334 and hac-335. The frames and the cut itself are this submission's, and are carried as the pipeline's output rather than as a second capability.

capabilities.title: Forensic Replay motion composition
capabilities.rationale: Renders the frozen thirty-second Forensic Replay as deterministic coded motion. What it contains is Interlock story and proof semantics: the eight-scene contract, the target geometry, the withheld-peer and evidence-ablation grammar, and presentation bindings read out of HAC-343 and HAC-330. None of that generalises, and generalising it into Studio would put product semantics in a rendering substrate. The reusable half — a deterministic state-at-time timeline over the display list — was earned by this composition and placed in hac-334's library instead, where it travels under that row's HARVEST_STUDIO disposition.

capabilities.title: Muted storyboard assembly
capabilities.rationale: Assembles one frozen 30-second storyboard for one submission. The reusable half is the asset registry, harvested separately; what remains is this submission's scene list.

capabilities.title: Provenance boundary gate
capabilities.rationale: A machine-checked manifest that refuses to let a manifest edit grant itself permission. Answers 'which repository may this change touch' with a gate rather than a README paragraph.

capabilities.title: Identity boundary gate
capabilities.rationale: Verifies one product's mark, vendored fonts and cockpit identity authority. Generalizes to nothing.

capabilities.title: Deterministic export naming
capabilities.rationale: Names exported assets deterministically from run and claim identity, so a filename cannot drift from what it depicts.

capabilities.title: Merge-gate matrix and hardening-receipt method
capabilities.rationale: One owner per failure class, values read back from the API rather than inferred from config, a bidirectional red/green proof per blocking gate, and a waiver register carrying owner, expiry and risk for what could not be proven.

capabilities.title: Harvest ledger and coverage gate
capabilities.rationale: Answers 'did any capability get dropped on the floor' with a coverage check rather than a prose assertion. Self-referential on purpose: this row is what stops the ledger from omitting itself.

findings.statement: Per-target locking preserves concurrency but can miss composition hazards spanning distinct targets; global locking preserves safety by eliminating concurrency. On a frozen sixteen-scenario corpus, Interlock withheld both hazardous compositions while retaining both safe parallel opportunities, and reversed its decision when the co-change evidence was removed.
findings.rationale: This is the submission's own bounded claim, already pinned in a frozen evidence packet with its scope boundary attached. Routing it to a Standard research issue would detach the claim from the corpus that bounds it.

findings.statement: BOUNDED_SEARCH_EXHAUSTED. No authentic natural worktree-composition fixture passed admission within the frozen universe and budget, so no transfer result was established.
findings.rationale: META-383's own completion routing names Fibery OQ-17 as the destination for its durable evidence, negative or contradiction. A negative is the finding most likely to be quietly dropped, and it is worth more than a positive from a search that had to be widened.

findings.statement: Most candidate roadmap decisions had no measurable baseline headroom, and no valid roadmap semantic established incremental agent-decision consequence.
findings.rationale: Same destination and same reasoning as META-383. Together these two record where not to invest.

provenance/manifest.json records it with status PLANNED. It was never built, has no paths, and therefore cannot receive a disposition. Recording one would assert work that did not happen.

notInInventory.reason: Lives on hac/316-agent-runtime-counterfactual (pushed 2026-08-30) and is not on main. Its disposition is DELETE_HACKATHON_ONLY, and no owner issue is required. HAC-316 is Canceled as [FAILED/PIVOTED]; the tree is 55 executable files — ADK agents, provisioning and teardown tooling — for an Agent Runtime topology that was abandoned. This is the same judgement already recorded for experiments/hac-325: keeping runnable provisioning for an abandoned architecture invites someone to run it. The provenance survives on the pushed branch, which is what HAC-341 means by 'failed/pivoted historical provenance only'; nothing on main references the path.
notInInventory.entersInventoryWhen: never — DELETE is the decision. It would need a row only if the tree were landed on main, which this disposition declines.

notInInventory.reason: Lives on origin/hac/339-agent-gateway-forensics and is not on main. Its disposition is HARVEST_INTEGRATIONS under META-330, recorded there 2026-08-30. Eleven files, zero executables: a current Google support matrix for the Agent Runtime / Agent Gateway topology, a hypothesis matrix narrowing the HAC-325 TLS root cause, and a designed one-shot probe. Unlike hac-325 this is not runnable machinery for an abandoned path, so the DELETE rationale does not reach it — it is environment-evidence about the Google adapter boundary, which is META-330's scope. HAC-338 remains the sprint-local re-audit issue; META-330 is the post-window durable home.

Lives on origin/hac/340-minimal-gemini-adk-cloud-path and is not on main. Its disposition is HARVEST_INTEGRATIONS under META-330, recorded there 2026-08-30. It is the Gemini + ADK agent, Cloud Run deployment and frozen evidence for the traversal META-330 names as its entry proof, and the thinnest honest ADK adapter question is the one it answers. Two constraints travel with it: experiments/hac-340/evidence carries the unredacted identifiers and must not be published — experiments/hac-342 is the public derivative and the only judge-facing form; and those bytes are the referent of the hac-342 sourcePacketSha256 commitment, so the tree must be retained, never deleted, or that commitment becomes permanently uncheckable.

Lives on origin/hac/335-veo-hero and is not on main. Its disposition is HARVEST_STUDIO under HAC-324 — inherited, not new: the media coverage root is children mode, so media/hac-335 is the covered unit and the existing judge-package-and-asset-registry row already claims it. A separate row would double-claim the path and turn the gate red. Recorded here only because the subtree is not yet on main and an absence should never read as an oversight.
notInInventory.entersInventoryWhen: the HAC-335 veo-hero branch merges — at which point it is already claimed by judge-package-and-asset-registry and needs no new row
